description: This dashboard tracks IP overlap risk and diversity health across the fleet. It helps protect isolation quality and identify concentration problems early.

panels.description: Counts the current number of duplicated outbound IP groups for the selected Proxy Status and City filters. Each value is one outbound IP currently shared by 2 or more selected phones. Lower is healthier; zero means the selected phones do not currently share any outbound IPs.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) as value FROM (
  SELECT last_ip
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
  AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY last_ip
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) as dup_ips

panels.title: Duplicate IPs (shared by 2+ phones)

panels.description: Counts selected phones currently affected by duplicate IPs. A phone is included when its current outbound IP is also used by at least one other selected phone. This is a current-state impact count, not a historical count over the dashboard time range.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(*) as value
FROM proxies
WHERE TRIM(city) IN ($city)
AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
AND last_ip IN (
  SELECT last_ip
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
  AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY last_ip
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)

panels.title: Affected Phones (sharing an IP)

panels.description: Shows the largest current duplicate cluster in the selected cities. The value is the maximum number of selected phones sharing one outbound IP. A high value means a single IP is concentrated across many phones and should be prioritized for investigation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT MAX(phone_count) as value FROM (
  SELECT last_ip, COUNT(*) as phone_count
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
  AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY last_ip
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) as counts

panels.title: Max Phones Sharing One IP

panels.description: Counts how many of the selected cities currently have at least one duplicated outbound IP. This helps show whether duplicate exposure is isolated to one city or spread across the selected city set.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT city) as value
FROM proxies
WHERE city IS NOT NULL
AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
AND last_ip IN (
  SELECT last_ip
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
  AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY last_ip
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)

panels.title: Cities with Duplicate IPs

panels.description: Ranks currently duplicated outbound IPs by the number of selected phones using each IP. Taller bars identify the shared IP groups with the largest current phone impact.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT last_ip, COUNT(*) as phone_count
FROM proxies
WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
GROUP BY last_ip
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY phone_count DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Top Duplicate IPs by Phone Count

panels.description: Ranks selected city/state locations by current duplicate impact. affected_phones counts selected phones on duplicate IPs; duplicate_ips counts distinct shared IP groups in that city/state. Use this to identify the locations where cleanup has the largest immediate impact.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(IFNULL(city,'Unknown'), ', ', IFNULL(state,'')) as city_label,
  COUNT(*) as affected_phones,
  COUNT(DISTINCT last_ip) as duplicate_ips
FROM proxies
WHERE TRIM(city) IN ($city)
AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
AND last_ip IN (
  SELECT last_ip
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
  AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY last_ip
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)
GROUP BY city, state
ORDER BY affected_phones DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Cities with Most IP-Sharing Phones

panels.description: Maps current duplicate-IP impact for selected cities using device latitude and longitude. The map shows where affected phones and duplicate IP groups are geographically concentrated. Devices with missing or unusable coordinates are grouped into the fallback location marker.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN is_unknown_location = 1 THEN 'No Location (N/A)'
    WHEN city_label IS NULL AND state_label IS NULL THEN 'Unknown, '
    ELSE CONCAT(IFNULL(city_label, 'Unknown'), ', ', IFNULL(state_label, ''))
  END as location_label,
  avg_lat,
  avg_lon,
  affected_phones,
  duplicate_ips
FROM (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN p.latitude IS NULL
        OR p.longitude IS NULL
        OR p.city IS NULL
        OR p.city = ''
        OR LOWER(p.city) = 'n/a'
        OR p.state IS NULL
        OR p.state = ''
        OR LOWER(p.state) = 'n/a'
      THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END as is_unknown_location,
    AVG(
      CASE
        WHEN p.latitude IS NULL
          OR p.longitude IS NULL
          OR p.city IS NULL
          OR p.city = ''
          OR LOWER(p.city) = 'n/a'
          OR p.state IS NULL
          OR p.state = ''
          OR LOWER(p.state) = 'n/a'
        THEN 32.5
        ELSE p.latitude
      END
    ) as avg_lat,
    AVG(
      CASE
        WHEN p.latitude IS NULL
          OR p.longitude IS NULL
          OR p.city IS NULL
          OR p.city = ''
          OR LOWER(p.city) = 'n/a'
          OR p.state IS NULL
          OR p.state = ''
          OR LOWER(p.state) = 'n/a'
        THEN -119.5
        ELSE p.longitude
      END
    ) as avg_lon,
    COUNT(*)                  as affected_phones,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.last_ip) as duplicate_ips,
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(GROUP_CONCAT(p.city  ORDER BY p.city  SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1) as city_label,
    SUBSTRING_INDEX(GROUP_CONCAT(p.state ORDER BY p.state SEPARATOR ','), ',', 1) as state_label
  FROM proxies p
  WHERE TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR p.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
    AND p.last_ip IN (
      SELECT last_ip
      FROM proxies
      WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
      AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
      AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
      GROUP BY last_ip
      HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
    )
  GROUP BY
    CASE
      WHEN p.latitude IS NULL
        OR p.longitude IS NULL
        OR p.city IS NULL
        OR p.city = ''
        OR LOWER(p.city) = 'n/a'
        OR p.state IS NULL
        OR p.state = ''
        OR LOWER(p.state) = 'n/a'
      THEN 'unknown'
      ELSE CONCAT(ROUND(p.latitude, 1), ':', ROUND(p.longitude, 1))
    END,
    CASE
      WHEN p.latitude IS NULL
        OR p.longitude IS NULL
        OR p.city IS NULL
        OR p.city = ''
        OR LOWER(p.city) = 'n/a'
        OR p.state IS NULL
        OR p.state = ''
        OR LOWER(p.state) = 'n/a'
      THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
) t
ORDER BY affected_phones DESC

panels.title: Geographic Distribution of Duplicate IP Phones

panels.description: Lists one row per currently shared outbound IP in the selected cities. phone_count is the number of selected phones sharing that IP; active_count and inactive_count split the devices by status; phones, device_ids, cities, and countries provide the investigation details.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  last_ip,
  COUNT(*) as phone_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN proxy_status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as active_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN proxy_status = 'inactive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as inactive_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name SEPARATOR ', ') as phones,
  GROUP_CONCAT(device_id ORDER BY name SEPARATOR ', ') as device_ids,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT IFNULL(city,'?') ORDER BY city SEPARATOR ', ') as cities,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT IFNULL(country,'?') ORDER BY country SEPARATOR ', ') as countries
FROM proxies
WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
GROUP BY last_ip
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY phone_count DESC, last_ip

panels.title: Duplicate IPs — Summary (one row per shared IP)

panels.description: Server-focused duplicate analysis for the selected cities. These panels show which inferred server labels and server pairs are most involved in duplicate IP exposure.
panels.title: Server-Based Duplicate Analysis

panels.description: Shows current duplicate-IP impact by inferred server label for selected cities. duplicate_ips counts distinct shared IPs involving that server; affected_phones counts selected phones on those duplicated IPs. Higher values identify servers contributing more duplicate exposure.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  server,
  COUNT(DISTINCT last_ip) as duplicate_ips,
  COUNT(*) as affected_phones
FROM (
  SELECT
    last_ip,
    CASE
      WHEN UPPER(name) REGEXP '^S[0-9]+' THEN CONCAT('S', SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(name), 'P', 1), 'S', -1))
      ELSE 'Unknown'
    END as server
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
  AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  AND last_ip IN (
    SELECT last_ip
    FROM proxies
    WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
    AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
    GROUP BY last_ip
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
  )
) AS t
GROUP BY server
ORDER BY duplicate_ips DESC, affected_phones DESC

panels.title: Duplicate IPs Per Server

panels.description: Splits the latest duplicate-IP exposure by server into within-server and cross-server collisions for selected cities. within_server_dup_ips means the duplicate IP appears only on one inferred server; cross_server_dup_ips means the same IP spans more than one server label.

targets.rawSql:
WITH selected_cities AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT TRIM(city) AS city
  FROM proxies
  WHERE TRIM(city) IN ($city)
), latest AS (
  SELECT MAX(r.captured_at) AS captured_at
  FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_rows r
  WHERE r.proxy_status_scope = '${proxy_status}'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM selected_cities c
      WHERE LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ','), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
        OR LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ' | '), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
    )
), filtered_rows AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT r.captured_at, r.proxy_status_scope, r.last_ip
  FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_rows r
  JOIN latest l ON l.captured_at = r.captured_at
  WHERE r.proxy_status_scope = '${proxy_status}'
    AND EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM selected_cities c
      WHERE LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ','), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
        OR LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ' | '), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
    )
), ip_server_counts AS (
  SELECT s.last_ip, COUNT(DISTINCT TRIM(s.server_label)) AS distinct_servers_on_ip
  FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_servers s
  JOIN filtered_rows r
    ON r.captured_at = s.captured_at
    AND r.proxy_status_scope = s.proxy_status_scope
    AND r.last_ip = s.last_ip
  GROUP BY s.last_ip
)
SELECT
  TRIM(s.server_label) AS server,
  SUM(CASE WHEN c.distinct_servers_on_ip = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS within_server_dup_ips,
  SUM(CASE WHEN c.distinct_servers_on_ip > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS cross_server_dup_ips
FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_servers s
JOIN filtered_rows r
  ON r.captured_at = s.captured_at
  AND r.proxy_status_scope = s.proxy_status_scope
  AND r.last_ip = s.last_ip
JOIN ip_server_counts c ON c.last_ip = s.last_ip
WHERE s.proxy_status_scope = '${proxy_status}'
GROUP BY TRIM(s.server_label)
ORDER BY (within_server_dup_ips + cross_server_dup_ips) DESC, server

panels.title: Within vs Cross-Server Duplicate IPs Per Server

panels.description: Ranks inferred server pairs that currently share duplicated IPs among selected-city phones. shared_ips is the number of distinct outbound IPs seen on both servers in the pair. High values point to server combinations that may need routing, carrier, or allocation review.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  server_pair,
  COUNT(DISTINCT last_ip) as shared_ips
FROM (
  SELECT
    a.last_ip,
    CONCAT(
      LEAST(
        CASE WHEN UPPER(a.name) REGEXP '^S[0-9]+' THEN CONCAT('S', SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(a.name), 'P', 1), 'S', -1)) ELSE 'Unknown' END,
        CASE WHEN UPPER(b.name) REGEXP '^S[0-9]+' THEN CONCAT('S', SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(b.name), 'P', 1), 'S', -1)) ELSE 'Unknown' END
      ),
      ' vs ',
      GREATEST(
        CASE WHEN UPPER(a.name) REGEXP '^S[0-9]+' THEN CONCAT('S', SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(a.name), 'P', 1), 'S', -1)) ELSE 'Unknown' END,
        CASE WHEN UPPER(b.name) REGEXP '^S[0-9]+' THEN CONCAT('S', SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(b.name), 'P', 1), 'S', -1)) ELSE 'Unknown' END
      )
    ) as server_pair
  FROM proxies a
  JOIN proxies b ON a.last_ip = b.last_ip AND a.device_id < b.device_id
  WHERE a.last_ip IS NOT NULL AND a.last_ip != ''
    AND TRIM(a.city) IN ($city)
    AND TRIM(b.city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR a.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR b.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
) as pairs
GROUP BY server_pair
ORDER BY shared_ips DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Top Server Pairs Sharing IPs

panels.description: Groups current duplicate-IP impact by state for the selected City filter. duplicate_devices counts selected phones in that state on duplicated IPs; duplicate_ips counts distinct shared IPs. Use this to see whether selected city exposure clusters under specific states.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  s.state_label AS state,
  COUNT(*) AS duplicate_devices,
  COUNT(DISTINCT s.last_ip) AS duplicate_ips
FROM (
  SELECT
    p.last_ip,
    CASE
      WHEN p.state IS NULL OR TRIM(p.state) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(p.state)) = 'n/a'
      THEN 'unknown_state'
      ELSE LOWER(TRIM(p.state))
    END AS state_key,
    CASE
      WHEN p.state IS NULL OR TRIM(p.state) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(p.state)) = 'n/a'
      THEN 'Unknown State'
      ELSE TRIM(p.state)
    END AS state_label
  FROM proxies p
  JOIN (
    SELECT last_ip
    FROM proxies
    WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
      AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
      AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
    GROUP BY last_ip
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
  ) dup ON p.last_ip = dup.last_ip
  WHERE TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR p.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
) s
GROUP BY s.state_key, s.state_label
ORDER BY duplicate_devices DESC, duplicate_ips DESC
LIMIT 30

panels.title: Duplicate IP Impact by State

panels.description: Shows detailed current duplicate-IP evidence for selected cities. Each row is one shared IP with involved locations, inferred server labels, total phones on the IP, phone names, and device IDs. Use this table as the operational drill-down for follow-up.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  x.last_ip,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT x.location ORDER BY x.location SEPARATOR ' | ') AS location,
  MAX(dup.all_servers_on_ip) AS all_servers_on_ip,
  MAX(dup.phones_on_same_ip) AS phones_on_same_ip,
  MAX(dup.sibling_phones) AS sibling_phones,
  GROUP_CONCAT(x.name ORDER BY x.name SEPARATOR ' | ') AS phone_names,
  GROUP_CONCAT(x.device_id ORDER BY x.name SEPARATOR ' | ') AS device_ids
FROM (
  SELECT
    p.name,
    p.device_id,
    p.last_ip,
    p.proxy_status,
    CONCAT_WS(', ', NULLIF(TRIM(p.city), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(p.state), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(p.country), '')) AS location
  FROM proxies p
  WHERE p.last_ip IS NOT NULL AND p.last_ip != ''
    AND TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR p.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
) x
JOIN (
  SELECT
    last_ip,
    COUNT(*) AS phones_on_same_ip,
    GROUP_CONCAT(
      DISTINCT CASE WHEN UPPER(name) REGEXP '^S[0-9]+' THEN CONCAT('S', SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(name), 'P', 1), 'S', -1)) ELSE 'Unknown' END
      ORDER BY CASE WHEN UPPER(name) REGEXP '^S[0-9]+' THEN CAST(SUBSTRING_INDEX(SUBSTRING_INDEX(UPPER(name), 'P', 1), 'S', -1) AS UNSIGNED) ELSE 999999 END
      SEPARATOR ', '
    ) AS all_servers_on_ip,
    GROUP_CONCAT(name ORDER BY name SEPARATOR ' | ') AS sibling_phones
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
    AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY last_ip
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
) dup ON x.last_ip = dup.last_ip
GROUP BY x.last_ip
ORDER BY MAX(dup.phones_on_same_ip) DESC, x.last_ip

panels.title: Cross-Server Duplicate IP — Per-Phone Detail

panels.description: Breaks duplicate devices down by selected city and IP. Each row is one city/IP pair where 2 or more selected phones share the same outbound IP, with phone names and device IDs included for direct investigation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  x.city_label AS city,
  x.last_ip,
  COUNT(*) AS duplicate_devices,
  GROUP_CONCAT(x.name ORDER BY x.name SEPARATOR ' | ') AS names,
  GROUP_CONCAT(x.device_id ORDER BY x.name SEPARATOR ', ') AS device_ids
FROM (
  SELECT
    p.last_ip,
    p.device_id,
    p.name,
    CASE
      WHEN p.city IS NULL OR TRIM(p.city) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(p.city)) = 'n/a'
      THEN 'Unknown City'
      ELSE TRIM(p.city)
    END AS city_label,
    CASE
      WHEN p.city IS NULL OR TRIM(p.city) = '' OR LOWER(TRIM(p.city)) = 'n/a'
      THEN 'unknown_city'
      ELSE LOWER(TRIM(p.city))
    END AS city_key
  FROM proxies p
  WHERE p.last_ip IS NOT NULL AND p.last_ip != ''
    AND TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR p.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
) x
GROUP BY x.city_key, x.city_label, x.last_ip
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY duplicate_devices DESC, x.city_label ASC, x.last_ip ASC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Duplicate Devices by City + IP (Names, IDs)

panels.description: City comparison section controlled by the City variable. Use it to compare current duplicate exposure across any selected cities without editing the dashboard SQL.
panels.title: Selected Cities — Duplicate IP Comparison

panels.description: Compares current duplicate-IP exposure across selected cities. total_phones is the selected device count per city; phones_sharing_ip is how many are currently on duplicate IPs; duplicate_rate_pct normalizes that impact by city size; max_phones_per_dup_ip shows the largest duplicate cluster in that city.

targets.rawSql:
WITH dup_ips AS (
  SELECT last_ip
  FROM proxies
  WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
  AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY last_ip
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
),
city_stats AS (
  SELECT
    TRIM(p.city) AS city,
    COUNT(*) AS total_phones,
    SUM(CASE WHEN d.last_ip IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS phones_sharing_ip,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d.last_ip IS NOT NULL THEN p.last_ip END) AS duplicate_ips
  FROM proxies p
  LEFT JOIN dup_ips d ON p.last_ip = d.last_ip
  WHERE ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  AND TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
  GROUP BY TRIM(p.city)
),
max_per_ip AS (
  SELECT TRIM(p2.city) AS city, MAX(cnt.phones_per_ip) AS max_phones_per_dup_ip
  FROM (
    SELECT last_ip, COUNT(*) AS phones_per_ip
    FROM proxies
    WHERE last_ip IS NOT NULL AND last_ip != ''
    AND TRIM(city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
    GROUP BY last_ip
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
  ) cnt
  JOIN proxies p2 ON p2.last_ip = cnt.last_ip
  WHERE TRIM(p2.city) IN ($city)
  GROUP BY TRIM(p2.city)
)
SELECT
  c.city,
  c.total_phones,
  c.phones_sharing_ip,
  c.duplicate_ips,
  ROUND(100.0 * c.phones_sharing_ip / NULLIF(c.total_phones, 0), 1) AS duplicate_rate_pct,
  IFNULL(m.max_phones_per_dup_ip, 0) AS max_phones_per_dup_ip
FROM city_stats c
LEFT JOIN max_per_ip m ON c.city = m.city
ORDER BY duplicate_rate_pct DESC

panels.title: City Comparison — Duplicate IP Summary

panels.description: Lists current duplicate IPs separately for each selected city. Each row is one city/IP pair with phones_sharing, active/inactive counts, phone names, and device IDs. Use this to identify exactly which devices are driving each city's duplicate rate.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  TRIM(p.city) AS city,
  p.last_ip,
  COUNT(*) AS phones_sharing,
  SUM(CASE WHEN p.proxy_status = 'active' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN p.proxy_status = 'inactive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inactive_count,
  GROUP_CONCAT(p.name ORDER BY p.name SEPARATOR ' | ') AS phone_names,
  GROUP_CONCAT(p.device_id ORDER BY p.name SEPARATOR ', ') AS device_ids
FROM proxies p
WHERE p.last_ip IS NOT NULL AND p.last_ip != ''
AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
AND TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
GROUP BY TRIM(p.city), p.last_ip
HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
ORDER BY TRIM(p.city), phones_sharing DESC

panels.title: Duplicate IPs — Per-City Detail

panels.description: Daily trend section for selected cities. These panels compare historical duplicate intensity and rotation activity so you can see whether duplicate IP exposure is improving, worsening, or moving with rotation volume.
panels.title: City Trends — Daily (Selected Cities)

panels.description: Shows daily unique duplicate IP count per selected city. If the same duplicate IP appears in many scans on the same day, it is counted once for that city/day. This represents unique daily duplicate IP coverage, not repeated scan appearances.

targets.rawSql:
WITH selected_cities AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT TRIM(city) AS city
  FROM proxies
  WHERE TRIM(city) IN ($city)
)
SELECT
  UNIX_TIMESTAMP(DATE(r.captured_at)) AS time_sec,
  c.city AS metric,
  COUNT(DISTINCT r.last_ip) AS value
FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_rows r
JOIN selected_cities c
  ON LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ','), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
  OR LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ' | '), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
WHERE r.captured_at >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  AND r.proxy_status_scope = '${proxy_status}'
  AND r.last_ip != '__snapshot_empty__'
GROUP BY UNIX_TIMESTAMP(DATE(r.captured_at)), c.city
ORDER BY time_sec, metric

panels.title: Duplicate IPs per Day — Selected Cities

panels.description: Shows daily IP change events per selected city from proxy_requests_daily_summary. Use this with duplicate-IP trends to see whether higher rotation activity aligns with fewer duplicates, more churn, or no visible improvement.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
  UNIX_TIMESTAMP(s.day) AS time_sec,
  TRIM(p.city) AS metric,
  SUM(s.ip_change_count) AS value
FROM proxy_requests_daily_summary s
JOIN proxies p ON s.proxy_id = p.device_id
WHERE s.day >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  AND TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
  AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR p.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
GROUP BY UNIX_TIMESTAMP(s.day), TRIM(p.city)
ORDER BY time_sec, metric

panels.title: IP Rotation Events per Day — Selected Cities

panels.title: Selected Cities — Duplicate Comparison

panels.description: Compares 30-day duplicate frequency for all eligible devices in each selected city. total_devices shows city cohort size; scans_with_duplicates and duplicate_scan_rate_pct show how often that city had any duplicate in snapshot scans; daily_unique_duplicate_ip_total counts each duplicate IP once per city/day; scan observation fields describe repeated sightings across scans.

targets.rawSql:
WITH selected_cities AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT TRIM(city) AS city
  FROM proxies
  WHERE TRIM(city) IN ($city)
), city_sizes AS (
  SELECT
    TRIM(p.city) AS city,
    COUNT(*) AS total_devices
  FROM proxies p
  WHERE p.city IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(p.city) != ''
    AND TRIM(p.city) IN ($city)
    AND ('${proxy_status}' = 'all' OR p.proxy_status = '${proxy_status}')
  GROUP BY TRIM(p.city)
), scan_totals AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT captured_at) AS total_scans
  FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_rows
  WHERE proxy_status_scope = '${proxy_status}'
    AND captured_at >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
), duplicate_rows AS (
  SELECT
    r.captured_at,
    r.last_ip,
    r.phones_on_same_ip,
    c.city
  FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_rows r
  JOIN selected_cities c
    ON LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ','), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
    OR LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ' | '), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
  WHERE r.proxy_status_scope = '${proxy_status}'
    AND r.captured_at >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
    AND r.last_ip != '__snapshot_empty__'
), city_scans AS (
  SELECT
    city,
    captured_at,
    COUNT(DISTINCT last_ip) AS duplicate_ips_in_scan,
    SUM(phones_on_same_ip) AS affected_phone_observations_in_scan
  FROM duplicate_rows
  GROUP BY city, captured_at
)
SELECT
  s.city,
  s.total_devices,
  COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT c.captured_at), 0) AS scans_with_duplicates,
  MAX(t.total_scans) AS total_scans,
  COALESCE(ROUND(COUNT(DISTINCT c.captured_at) * 100.0 / NULLIF(MAX(t.total_scans), 0), 2), 0) AS duplicate_scan_rate_pct,
  COALESCE(SUM(c.duplicate_ips_in_scan), 0) AS duplicate_ip_observations,
  COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(c.duplicate_ips_in_scan), 2), 0) AS avg_duplicate_ips_when_hit,
  COALESCE(MAX(c.duplicate_ips_in_scan), 0) AS peak_duplicate_ips_in_scan,
  COALESCE(ROUND(AVG(c.affected_phone_observations_in_scan), 2), 0) AS avg_affected_phone_observations_when_hit
FROM city_sizes s
CROSS JOIN scan_totals t
LEFT JOIN city_scans c ON c.city = s.city
GROUP BY s.city, s.total_devices
ORDER BY duplicate_scan_rate_pct DESC, s.city

panels.title: All Devices Duplicate Frequency — Selected Cities

panels.description: Shows daily unique duplicate IPs for each selected city. Repeated sightings of the same duplicate IP during the same day count once for that city, so the line represents daily unique duplicate IP volume rather than scan-level repetition.

targets.rawSql:
WITH selected_cities AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT TRIM(city) AS city
  FROM proxies
  WHERE TRIM(city) IN ($city)
), duplicate_rows AS (
  SELECT
    DATE(r.captured_at) AS scan_day,
    r.last_ip,
    c.city
  FROM duplicate_ip_snapshot_rows r
  JOIN selected_cities c
    ON LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ','), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
    OR LOCATE(CONCAT(' | ', c.city, ' | '), CONCAT(' | ', COALESCE(r.location, ''), ' | ')) > 0
  WHERE r.proxy_status_scope = '${proxy_status}'
    AND r.captured_at >= DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
    AND r.last_ip != '__snapshot_empty__'
)
SELECT
  UNIX_TIMESTAMP(scan_day) AS time_sec,
  city AS metric,
  COUNT(DISTINCT last_ip) AS value
FROM duplicate_rows
GROUP BY scan_day, city
ORDER BY time_sec, metric
